findings.message: The fix for the 200-row cap removed the limit but did not move the real filter into SQL. The SQL filters are now applied first, but 'who reviews it' still runs in JS: one `reviews()` call per row, each one querying `weekProjectIds`. The fetch has no bound at all, so get_change_requests with no status, or with a closed status, returns the tenant's whole history. That means one chain query per other person's request, and the full list goes into the model's context. The new test needs a 60 s timeout for only 250 rows. Fix: express the approver's scope in SQL (the week's project ids against the viewer's approvable projects, or `user_id = viewer`), then page the result with a limit and a cursor or `truncated` flag the caller can see.
findings.scenario: Tenant with 5,000 declined requests; an approver calls get_change_requests {status:'declined'} → about 5,000 sequential weekProjectIds queries, then a 5,000-item tool result. The chat turn times out or overflows the model context, where before it returned a capped list.

findings.message: The AC-52 variant test calls `config.events.signIn` with an Auth.js message it builds by hand (`account: { amax: after }`). It also passes `replaced` as a stub that returns `before`. That leaves the parts the fix depends on untested: Auth.js firing the event after `callbacks.signIn` puts `amax` on the Entra account, and `apps/web/auth.ts`'s `replaced = sessionStamp(await auth())` returning the browser's earlier session while a sign-in completes. If `auth()` there returned null or the new session, every case would still pass and no earlier session would be revoked. Fix: drive at least one real sign-in through the Auth.js handler (a credentials POST to /api/auth/callback/password carrying an earlier session cookie, and an Entra callback with a mocked token endpoint), and assert that the earlier session row ends.
findings.scenario: Break apps/web/auth.ts so `replaced` returns `undefined`. The switch.test cases still pass, but a real Entra or password switch leaves the earlier session alive.

findings.message: `failureNote` assumes any plain `Error` with no `cause` was written by this module, and passes its message on to the done card, the model and the audit `after`. Infrastructure errors don't fit that assumption. postgres-js throws its connection errors (CONNECTION_CLOSED, CONNECTION_DESTROYED, CONNECT_TIMEOUT, ECONNRESET) as plain `Error` objects with only a `code` and no cause, and those messages include the database host and port. The rest of the app already has one rule for this: `toolFailure` in packages/ai/src/gateway.ts maps a failure to a fixed phrase by error name or code and never uses the message. This change adds a second, looser classifier, so the two can disagree (B4). Fix: send module refusals through a dedicated class, such as `ToolError` (which `card.ts` already uses) or `ValidationError`, and keep only the messages of those classes. Everything else, including a plain `Error`, should map to the reference note. Add a postgres-js-style connection error to the table test.
findings.scenario: The pool drops during approve_weeks. The driver throws `new Error('write CONNECTION_CLOSED db.internal:5432')` with code CONNECTION_CLOSED and no cause. `failureNote` treats it as ours, so the person's row says 'write CONNECTION_CLOSED db.internal:5432' on the done card, in the model's context and in the audit `after`.

findings.message: `KNOWN_UNNAMED` lets 15 existing columns through the new per-column retention check. Several hold personal data that erasure and anonymisation never reach: `notifications.preference.email`, `compliance.incident.notify_by`, `presales.activity.note`, `presales.stage_change.note`, `presales.suggestion.client_name` and `career.history.detail`. These columns predate this change. They are tracked only in a follow-ups note, and no change owns them. Fix: open a change per module to add the columns to its retention entries, then remove them from the list.
findings.scenario: An approved erasure request for a person whose email is in notifications.preference.email → the request completes, and the email stays in that column.

findings.message: The new per-column check only looks at tables that already have a named personal column (`found.has(t)`). A jsonb column can copy a note or name into a table whose only person column is a pseudonymous `user_id`/`person_id`. That table is never in `found`, so the check needs no retention entry for it and never flags the jsonb column. This is the 'jsonb copies of personal columns' variant from the round-1 finding, still open for that table shape. Fix: also flag json/jsonb columns in tables that have no retention entry, or require an explicit opt-out.
findings.scenario: `create table x.audit_copy (id uuid, user_id uuid, snapshot jsonb)` where `snapshot` holds an entry's note → the check passes with no retention entry, and erasure never clears the note copy.

findings.message: The project check on a move is skipped when `viewerOf(ctx)` returns nothing (`if (v && !mayMove(...))`). The card-side check in `checked()` always runs. So a context with no viewer (a job or system context) can move an entry to any project. Fix: refuse when there is no viewer (fail closed) instead of skipping the check.
findings.scenario: decideRequest runs under a job context with no viewer and applies a request that moves hours to a project nobody approved → the move is applied with no scope check.
